chapter_title: The Chapter of the Name of the Fathers
chapter_note: After a brief dialogue frame (¶1–2), the chapter gives a compact, systematic cosmological definition of why multiple divine beings can be called “father”: each is “father” relative to his own “greatness” (a corresponding realm/vehicle in which he is established). No pastoral/application turn and no NT citation overlay; “Jesus the Splendour” functions as a cosmological entity.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Formulaic hagiographic dialogue frame (“Once again the enlightener speaks to his disciples”) introducing the question.
Petition/Q&A apparatus (“We beseech you, our master…”) characteristic of the compiled Kephalaia frame, not the underlying teaching exposition.

paragraphs.core_text: Now, the Father, who is the first established thing, shall be called ‘the Father of Greatness’. His greatness is the great earth where he lives, he being established in it [...] the essence of the light that swathes all the rich gods and the angels and the dwellings [...] is set over it.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue attribution frame: “Then he speaks to his disciples:” (Kephalaia hagiographic container).
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core correspondential/cosmological exposition: “Father” defined by ontological primacy (“first established thing”) and by his “greatness” as a realm (“great earth”) with other cosmic beings/dwellings ordered under an “essence of the light.”

paragraphs.core_text: Furthermore, they shall call the Third Ambassador ‘father’. His greatness is the light ship of living fire wherein he lives, he being established in it.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Systematic extension of the same internal cosmos→cosmos mapping: title “father” + corresponding “greatness” as a specific cosmic vehicle/realm (“light ship of living fire”). No institutional pointing.

paragraphs.core_text: Once again, Jesus the Splendour shall himself also be called ‘father’. His greatness is the ship of living waters where he lives, he being established in it.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Continues the same structured teaching. “Jesus the Splendour” is used as a Manichaean cosmological being (not a Gospel citation), with his “greatness” defined as a cosmic ship/realm (“living waters”).
